blogs.title: What Is a 1.58-bit LLM? A Friendly Guide to Ternary Weights
blogs.description: Explain the leap from 16-bit to 1.58-bit models using plain language. Cover how ternary weights {-1, 0, +1} work, why adding zero matters for feature filtering, and how BitNet b1.58 keeps quality comparable to full-precision models while slashing compute and memory.

blogs.title: Speed, Memory, Energy: How BitNet b1.58 Rewrites the Efficiency Playbook
blogs.description: Walk through the headline gains: 2.4–4.1x inference speedups, 3.3–3.6x lower GPU memory, and up to 71x arithmetic energy savings. Use simple analogies for matrix multiplication with additions only, and show why efficiency improves further as models get larger.

blogs.title: From Quantization to Foundation: Training 1.58-bit Models From Scratch
blogs.description: Contrast post-training quantization with BitNet b1.58’s train-from-scratch approach. Demystify the absmean rounding trick, 8-bit activations without zero-point, and why these choices preserve accuracy. Summarize results showing parity with FP16 from 3B parameters and up.

blogs.title: The New Scaling Law: Bigger Models, Smaller Bills
blogs.description: Unpack the paper’s proposed scaling behavior linking model size to cost. Explain the practical equivalences (e.g., 13B b1.58 vs 3B FP16) and how latency, memory, and energy scale in the 1.58-bit regime. Discuss what this means for roadmap planning and capacity forecasting.

blogs.title: Under the Hood: LLaMA-Compatible Design That Just Works
blogs.description: Describe how BitNet b1.58 swaps nn.Linear for BitLinear while staying LLaMA-alike with RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, and no biases. Show why this makes integration easy with Hugging Face, vLLM, and llama.cpp, and what kernel support (e.g., 2-bit kernels) means for deployment.

blogs.title: Throughput Wins at Scale: What 70B Models Teach Us
blogs.description: Dive into the 70B two-GPU results: up to 11x larger batch sizes and 8.9x higher throughput than FP16 baselines. Explain pipeline parallelism in simple terms and why lower memory bandwidth and lighter compute let 1.58-bit models serve more users per node.

blogs.title: Edge, Mobile, and Long Contexts: New Frontiers for 1.58-bit LLMs
blogs.description: Explore practical benefits beyond the datacenter: smaller KV caches via 8-bit activations enable longer contexts; reduced memory and CPU-friendly ops make on-device models realistic. Outline use cases from offline assistants to IoT reasoning and privacy-preserving apps.

blogs.title: MoE and Custom Chips: Building for a 1-bit Future
blogs.description: Explain why Mixture-of-Experts pairs naturally with 1.58-bit weights (less memory, lower interconnect traffic) and how this could shrink multi-node footprints. Discuss the opportunity for specialized hardware—add-only matrix engines and memory hierarchies tuned for ternary weights.
